region: Asia and Middle East, including Turkey
method: Conservative, sector-specific historical mapping. Year ceilings describe the available game node, not a uniform development year for the whole nation. Imported equipment can support bounded service knowledge but never automatically copies its supplier's industrial or strategic programme.

Does not inherit the parent or patron state's nuclear, strategic missile, satellite, advanced aircraft or heavy-weapon manufacturing catalogue.

exclusions: No operational Ohsumi or orbital-launch capability on 1 January 1970; launch was in February.

Fuel-fabrication foundations do not backdate 1972 commercial fuel factories, 1977 reprocessing, enrichment operation or nuclear weapons.

Tarapur is BWR, not Magnox/PWR: reactor1/reactor2 are not granted simply to imitate a missing BWR node.
No later Cheetah licence or Jaguar/Ajeet production; sounding rockets do not imply orbital-launch success.
No imported-mainframe-to-integrated-circuit equivalence.

ROJ.name: Rojava

exclusions: Conservative scenario fallback inferred from local 1970 institutions; no independent national programme is claimed.
Does not inherit the parent or patron state's nuclear, strategic missile, satellite, advanced aircraft or heavy-weapon manufacturing catalogue.

RYU.name: Ryukyu

exclusions: Conservative scenario fallback inferred from local 1970 institutions; no independent national programme is claimed.

SAU.name: Saudi Arabia

SIA.name: Thailand

exclusions: No F-5E, 1980s armoured programme, later nuclear power plans, national ballistic missile or broad high-technology industry.

SIK.name: Sikkim

exclusions: Conservative scenario fallback inferred from local 1970 institutions; no independent national programme is claimed.
Does not inherit the parent or patron state's nuclear, strategic missile, satellite, advanced aircraft or heavy-weapon manufacturing catalogue.

SIN.name: Singapore
SIN.rationale: Strong port, repair and developing manufacturing capacity with very recent army and air-defence institutions. The first commando unit existed by December 1969, but the force and local arms sector were still young.
exclusions: No operational Independence patrol craft before December 1970, missile boat force, frigate, modern MBT industry, advanced national fighter or strategic programme.
Later electronics, aerospace and shipbuilding achievements are not backdated to the independence-era force.

SRI.name: Ceylon (Sri Lanka)
SRI.rationale: Plantation economy with a useful civil administration, light industrial and power sector, but a small military mainly using older British types. Jet Provost experience supports only the basic light-jet family.
exclusions: No supersonic fighter industry, 1971 emergency acquisitions, modern frigates, missile boats, nuclear or strategic missiles.

SVN.name: Republic of Vietnam
SVN.rationale: US-supported forces have strong equipment familiarity and helicopter-based support despite a narrow wartime manufacturing base. Dalat provides retained research knowledge even though the reactor was in extended shutdown.
exclusions: No full American manufacturing, electronics or strategic-weapon inheritance.
No operating commercial nuclear station; Dalat remains a research facility in shutdown.
No later F-5E or post-1970 armour and air-force expansion.

SYE.name: People's Republic of Southern Yemen
SYE.rationale: Aden's port and inherited British facilities support modest engineering and military maintenance. The later Soviet-equipped force is not copied wholesale into the immediate post-independence starting position.
exclusions: No later MiG-21/modern tank expansion, advanced missile navy, domestic aerospace, nuclear or strategic missiles.

SYR.name: Syria
SYR.rationale: Developing civil infrastructure and heavily imported Soviet military equipment. Conventional operational familiarity is retained, while domestic industrial research remains modest.
exclusions: No later Scud deployment/production, chemical-warfare industrial programme, nuclear reactor, modern aircraft manufacture or post-1970 tank generations.

TAB.name: Tabaristan

TAB.rationale: Caspian Tabaristan receives local civil, agricultural and coastal-workshop knowledge, without central Iranian military research.
exclusions: Conservative scenario fallback inferred from local 1970 institutions; no independent national programme is claimed.

exclusions: No F-5E licensed-production programme, indigenous fighter, modern tank programme, semiconductor foundry or nuclear power plant at the cutoff.

exclusions: No post-1971 federal air force, Mirage combat fleet, modern MBT industry, nuclear or strategic missiles.

VIE.name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
VIE.rationale: Mobilised wartime workshops and Soviet/Chinese assistance support modern imported aircraft and missile operations. Their employment does not establish independent aviation, electronic or armour manufacturing capability.
exclusions: No inherited Dalat reactor: the site is in South Vietnam and was shut down from 1968.
